standard.title: Create texts using familiar language
standard.description: use words, familiar phrases and modelled language to create spoken, written and multimodal texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can communicate using modelled words and formulaic phrases (AC9LSF01) and respond to texts using gestures, images and words (AC9LS2C03). They have not yet created their own texts — they have only responded to or repeated modelled language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use familiar words, phrases and modelled language to create spoken, written and multimodal texts about themselves, familiar topics and imaginative subjects.

nodes.label: Creating texts about self
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create simple spoken and written texts about themselves — including profiles and descriptions — using familiar vocabulary and modelled sentence structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text about themselves using at least three target language elements using modelled structures.
nodes.typical_width: Create self-portraits, profiles and simple descriptions using modelled sentence structures — personal details, family members, preferences; use familiar vocabulary across personal domains; incorporate labels, captions and speech bubbles in multimodal formats.
wider: Extend a self-description beyond the modelled minimum — adding personal details not explicitly provided in the model
Create a bilingual text about themselves identifying where structures are parallel and where they differ
nodes.hinge_reason: Creating texts about self is the first production task requiring students to select and arrange language rather than repeat it. Students who cannot move from modelled repetition to basic personal production cannot progress to imaginative or informative text creation.

response_modes.reason: Text creation from modelled language requires students to transfer phrases from a model to their own personal content. Repeated creation tasks with varied personal content build the transferable production skill.

success_criteria: Creates a text about themselves with at least three target language elements using modelled structures
Produces at least one written or multimodal element (label, caption, speech bubble) alongside spoken text

nodes.label: Creating imaginative and informative multimodal texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create imaginative and informative multimodal texts — describing characters, places and familiar topics — using familiar vocabulary and adapted modelled language.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one multimodal text (spoken and visual, or written and visual) about a character, place or event using familiar target language.
nodes.typical_width: Create character descriptions, story re-enactments, simple informative texts and bilingual captions using familiar vocabulary; add captions to displays; substitute words to create alternative versions of known stories or songs.
wider: Substitute multiple elements to create a genuinely adapted version of a known story or song — changing character, setting and at least one action
Create a multimodal text across both imaginative and informative modes on the same topic — demonstrating flexible use of familiar language

response_modes.reason: Text creation skills develop through varied text types and purposes. Creating across informative and imaginative modes — and across modalities — builds flexible production capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Moving from personal texts to imaginative and informative creation signals students are using the target language for purposes beyond self-expression — a significant expansion of communicative range.
success_criteria: Creates at least one multimodal text combining visual and target language elements about an imaginative or informative topic
Uses adapted (not verbatim) modelled language in at least one creation — demonstrating flexibility beyond direct copying

nodes.label: Creating for real audiences and purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create texts that serve real communicative purposes for genuine audiences — including cards, bilingual captions, event materials and labelled displays.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one text for a genuine purpose or audience beyond the immediate classroom activity.
nodes.typical_width: Make bilingual cards for real occasions; add bilingual captions to school displays or event materials; label maps or community resources; create materials for genuine school events and celebrations.
wider: Create a bilingual text for a specified real audience — making deliberate choices about which language element to use for each audience need and explaining the choice
Create a text for a real occasion that is subsequently used — displayed, sent or performed — demonstrating the text fulfilled its communicative purpose

response_modes.reason: Creating for real audiences integrates all prior text creation work — personal expression (N1) and imaginative/informative production (N2) — and applies it for genuine communicative purpose.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating texts that are actually used — displayed, sent, performed — positions students as genuine language producers for a real community. This is the qualitative shift from classroom exercise to authentic communication.
success_criteria: Creates at least one text for a genuine purpose or audience outside the immediate classroom activity
The text communicates its intended meaning clearly — a real recipient could understand it without teacher explanation
